guarantees.claim: clear_in_out_status is directly assigned to ctrl_we_q.

data_in_new_d is reset to all zeros when data_in_load is true, all bits of data_in_qe_i are high, or clear_in_out_status is true; otherwise it accumulates writes as the bitwise OR of data_in_new_q and data_in_qe_i.
data_in_new is high when all bits of data_in_new_d are high.
data_out_read_d is reset to all zeros when all bits of data_out_read_q are high or clear_in_out_status is true; otherwise it accumulates reads as the bitwise OR of data_out_read_q and data_out_re_i.
data_out_read is high when all bits of data_out_read_d are high.

assumptions.claim: External logic must not set all bits of data_in_qe_i during normal write operations, because that pattern is reserved for clearing data input registers with random data.
assumptions.cond: when a write to data input registers occurs and not a clear operation.
assumptions.risk: If a legitimate write asserts all data_in_qe_i bits, data_in_new_d is cleared to zero, causing data_in_new to deassert early. This may cause downstream logic to miss the indication that new input data is ready.

assumptions.claim: When all bits of data_out_read_q are high (indicating all output registers have been read), external logic must not simultaneously assert any bit of data_out_re_i.
assumptions.risk: data_out_read_d is forced to zero, ignoring new read request. data_out_read remains low, and the read tracking state is cleared without recording the new read, potentially losing an output read event.

uncertain_points.claim: The condition `&data_in_qe_i` that resets data_in_new_d may also be triggered by a legitimate full‑word write to the data input registers, because all byte‑enable bits would be high.
uncertain_points.cond: a normal write that happens to set all bits of data_in_qe_i.
uncertain_points.risk: Write status clears prematurely; data_in_new never asserts for that write, causing the cipher core to miss new input data (data could be ignored or not loaded).

uncertain_points.claim: When data_out_read_q is all ones and a new read is requested in the same cycle, the read event is dropped because data_out_read_d is forced to zero.
uncertain_points.cond: simultaneous `&data_out_read_q == 1'b1` and any bit of `data_out_re_i` asserted.
uncertain_points.risk: A valid read operation is not reflected in data_out_read, potentially causing the system to believe no read occurred and leading to stale status or dropped read acknowledgements.

uncertain_points.claim: data_in_new and data_out_read assert only when ALL bits of the corresponding accumulation vector are high, indicating the entire register bank has been written/read. It is unclear whether partial accesses must also be detected.
uncertain_points.cond: when only a subset of register bytes are written or read.
uncertain_points.risk: If partial writes/reads are legal and expected, the tracking signals will never assert, stalling downstream logic that waits for data_in_new or data_out_read.
